author: reek
body: The peripheral lifecycle, done right. A UART is opened once, written twice, and closed once, threading the linear handle through each step. The handle is consumed and re-minted by every operation, so the exactly-once discipline holds across the whole sequence.

author: reek
body: The register writes are real memory-mapped stores (the base is inside mapped RAM), so this exercises the honest MMIO path, not a stub.

author: reek
body: The three adversarial counterparts are errors/hal-peripheral-leak, errors/hal-peripheral-double-release, and errors/hal-peripheral-use-after-close.
